quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: For motorcycle riders, eye protection is:

options.text: Required.
Not required, but recommended.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders must use proper eye protection when riding in Georgia.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front so you can use its lights to see farther ahead.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being hit from behind.
Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. You cannot see as well in the dark, so you need extra time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
Return to your original lane as soon as the truck is behind you.
Return to your original lane when you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing a truck, only return to your lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your head.
Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn by turning just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
Release the front brake immediately and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake right away and then re-apply it.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic rules apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
Are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. They make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Take time to get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: The greatest risk of conflict between a motorcycle and other traffic is:

options.text: On the highway.
At intersections.
On rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcycles and other vehicles. Be extra careful when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight through your lane when crossing angled railroad or trolley tracks. If you change your path angle, you may move into another lane and hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding over scored pavement in a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding over scored pavement in a work zone. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center of the lane, what happens?

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.
You should avoid this position.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more often than side mirrors. This position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, what formation should you use?

options.text: Single-file formation.
Pairs.
Staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: How should you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from a hazard, apply a small amount of pressure to the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on your left. Riding on the right side can be dangerous because the passing driver may re-enter your lane too quickly.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. What should motorcyclists do?

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
Do not worry about the oil and grease.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. The oily strip is usually less than two feet wide, so you can often stay to the left or right side and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When parked on the road, how should a motorcycle be positioned?

options.text: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
With no wheel or fender touching the curb.
Parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should be at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees from the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: Are helmets required when riding?

options.text: Yes, for all riders.
No, but they are recommended.
Only for inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear U.S. Department of Transportation-compliant helmets every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries if you crash.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, what should you do?

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.
Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect yourself.
questions.explanation: A sturdy riding jacket provides protection in a crash, no matter the weather. In hot weather, jackets also protect you from losing fluids. Many riding jackets are designed to prevent overheating.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road is divided ahead.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol you drink, and how fast you drink it. How often you drink does not affect your BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually provides adequate traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually gives enough traction to ride safely, except in the rain. The strip is about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time it takes to react if you need to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If traveling with a load, the load should be:

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: If you are not using saddlebags, secure your load as low as possible. Attaching a load to a sissy bar raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and can affect its balance.
